Analysis: Hypothesis 1 focuses on the singular inhibition of ENTPD2 to modulate the immunosuppressive adenosine pathway in hypoxic HCC and enhance PD-1/PD-L1 therapy. It benefits from a clearer, more direct mechanism that is more straightforward to experimentally validate, despite concerns about specificity and compensatory mechanisms. In contrast, Hypothesis 2 combines ENTPD2 inhibition with direct PD-1/PD-L1 blockade. While this dual approach is novel and potentially synergistic, it raises more issues surrounding mechanistic synergy, testability, and safety due to possible off‐target effects and redundancy in immune regulatory pathways. Overall, the simpler, more focused approach of Hypothesis 1 offers greater plausibility, testability, and safety.
